elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall...", covering both events and applying to all three limbs (a)-(c).

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months"; the request condition is not tied only to anticipated expiry, so it applies after every covered expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days, return all data submitted by or on behalf of Licensee or processed for Licensee under this Agreement (\"Licensee Data\")", running from the chapeau trigger of expiry or termination.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing" — deletion expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same chapeau: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Licensee Data within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met by the single inserted paragraph in Article XXI; the fallback is also satisfied a fortiori.

The insertion is a concise new clause for a genuinely missing provision; it adds no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra damages or procedural boilerplate, and the existing Article XXI text (including the Licensee-side ship-back and Licensor survival sentence) is retained verbatim with no deletions.

The self-contained definition of "Licensee Data" (data submitted by or on behalf of Licensee or processed for Licensee) is necessary because the Agreement defines only Licensor-side material (Licensed Technology, Documentation, Confidential Information); it leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.
No contradiction arises with the retained one-way ship-back obligation or with Article XX termination mechanics; the new obligations run in the opposite direction and sit alongside them.
Party direction is correct: obligations are imposed on Licensor (counterparty) in favour of Licensee (our client), and no new Vendor rights or exceptions are created.
